chapter: Reading, repertoire and New Orleans players
title: Blues singers: Udell Wilson and Willie Jackson
summary: Asked about blues, he recalls pianist Udell Wilson and singer Willie Jackson, and says he plays his own way.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: Well, we... You know, we looked at pictures so long, we ought to do a little more talking. I've hardly got started on these things. Yeah. Uh... I wanted to ask you, did you hear any blues around New Orleans?
Well, what do you mean? What kind of blues?
Just singers and stuff like that. Oh, uh... Just a... Plano... On the levee or someplace like that.
Well, when we were out at Spanish Forth... Mm-hmm. Uh... At the casino, there was an ice cream pole there. Mm-hmm. Right across the Tokyo Garden, you see. Uh... Udell Wilson played piano.

And, uh... Trying to think of the guy's name... That used to sing with him, and it was a waiter. He made some records. And later on... When I went to New York, he was playing... Oh. Singing with... At Small's Paradise.
You told me about him when I was here before. Yeah.
I can't think of his name. Willie Jackson.
Yeah, you told me about that.
He sang a lot of... A lot of good... I got some of his records in the back there. Yeah.

Well, he used to... You know... Up there in... In... In... In... In... In... In... In... In... In... In... In... In... In... In... In... In... In... In... In... In... In... In... because I like I like the way he phrases voice you know a certain certain people I like and certain people I didn't like you know and a lot of people were rave about so-and-so and if I didn't like about it would I have a chance to say what I like and what I don't like see that's why I want to play my drums my way the way I like to play and the way and I can make people happy playing with them and if they like the way I play great that's why that's why I play with
